key_insight: Multi-material topology optimization tailors structural stiffness and mass to shift natural frequencies away from targeted resonance-prone bands.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing material selection and spatial distribution offers a route to reduce resonance risk and improve structural reliability.
method: Use multivariate weight-based interpolation to optimize material selection and distribution.
Handle mode switching with an auxiliary scalar variable and individual eigenvalue constraints.
Compare fundamental-frequency maximization, adjacent-frequency gap maximization, and targeted-band exclusion using a smooth rational polynomial approximation.
evidence_signal: Numerical examples demonstrate the proposed method and compare three frequency-based optimization formulations; the abstract reports no quantitative gains or experimental validation.
watch_item: Free-vibration frequency placement alone does not establish vibration-amplitude reduction under realistic forcing and damping.
paper_title: Multi-Material Topology Optimization for Targeted Structural Dynamic Vibration Attenuation
